Duplicate the track so there are two identical tracks at the same time offset. Save the project to /home/user/Music/single.aup. task_grounding:
Audacity is open with /home/user/Music/single.wav loaded (a 3-second 440 Hz sine tone at amplitude 0.3, mono 44.1 kHz — peak around -10 dBFS).

Select all audio (Ctrl+A) and use Edit > Duplicate (Ctrl+D) to copy the selection into a new second track containing the same audio at the same time offset.

Save the project to /home/user/Music/single.aup via File > Save Project > Save Project As....

Also export the full mix (both tracks playing simultaneously, which sums the two identical copies) to /home/user/Music/doubled.wav using File > Export > Export as WAV... with 'WAV (Microsoft) signed 16-bit PCM' at 44100 Hz mono. Because both tracks are identical, the exported mix peak should be approximately 6 dB higher than the original track (~-4 dBFS instead of ~-10 dBFS). Accept any metadata dialog defaults.

verification.description: Peak is ~6 dB above original (two identical tracks sum to ~2x amplitude)
